title: The power of expectation: Effects of an open-label placebo intervention on pain processing and learned anticipation - an experimental fMRI study in fibromyalgia syndrome
summary:
Numerous studies have impressively demonstrated that treatment with placebos, i.e. medication without an actual active ingredient, can have clinically significant positive effects on various diseases, including pain. Surprisingly, these positive effects  also occur when the patient knows that the medication used is a placebo, i.e. when a so-called open-label placebo (OLP) is administered. The underlying mechanisms of this effect are primarily positive expectations of the treatment, which can contribute to substantial changes in the experience of pain and its processing in the brain. However, the exact mechanisms of action and possible influencing factors are still poorly understood and have never been addressed in patients sufferig from fibromyalgia (FMS).
The aim of the planned study is therefore to expand our understanding of the processing of unpleasant sensory sensations in the form of heat pain under the influence of an OLP treatment using brain imaging techniques (functional magnetic resonance imaging, fMRI) and behavioral research in a sample of patients with FMS and healthy women. We are also interested in the extent to which such treatment can interact with pain-related learning and memory processes in order to use these findings to create the basis for improved approaches to patient care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
FMS: confirmed diagnosis of fibromyalgia syndrome; 
All participants: BMI 18-30kg/m2
Exclusion criteria:
All participants: inflammatory, neuropathic or tumor pain; insufficient knowledge of German; noticeable cognitive impairments; limited legal capacity or custody by official order; use of opioids or sedatives; medication or drug dependence or abuse; illnesses that prevent lying quietly in the examination device for approx. 90 minutes (e.g. excessive pain, claustrophobia); metal parts or electrically working health aids in the body; large tattoos with metal particles

Healthy participants additionally: any acute or chronic physical illnesses; acute and chronic psychiatric diagnoses according to DSM-IV

Patients: acute or chronic physical illnesses other than FMS; severe psychiatric diagnoses according to DSM-IV (e.g. schizophrenia, bipolar disorder)
